gaps.explanation: 'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

gaps.sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.

gaps.sentence: Her annual ___ is reviewed every April.
gaps.hint: fixed regular pay for professional work, usually monthly
gaps.explanation: 'Salary' is fixed regular pay for professional or office work, usually paid monthly; 'wages' are usually weekly.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
gaps.hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
gaps.explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.

gaps.sentence: The hospital is ___ the city centre.
gaps.explanation: 'Near' is a preposition before a place; 'nearly' is an adverb of degree meaning almost; 'close' needs 'to'.
